correctness.rationale: With G=U diag(s)V^T, S=sum s_j, D=sum s_j^2 u_j^T H^-1u_j=2f, and t=tr(U^THU), direct expansion yields ratio 1-alpha(2-alpha*t)S^2/D. Because alpha<2/T_r, t<=T_r makes the progress term positive. For a marked column u_k, the matrix of squared orthogonal-completion coordinates is doubly stochastic, hence a linear functional alpha*t+J u_k^TH^-1 u_k is maximized at a permutation. The marked eigenvalue i and r-1 remaining largest eigenvalues produce alpha*T_{r,i}+J/lambda_i<=2 for J=min_i lambda_i(2-alpha T_{r,i}). Choosing maximum H^-1 frame diagonal and using D<=dmax sum s_j^2<=dmax S^2 implies the exact q_r. A rank-r eigenframe with singular values 1,eps,...,eps reaches each extremal branch in the limit, and positive eps ensures strict nonattainment for r>1. Rank 1 is attained. q_{r+1}>q_r at common allowable steps; positivity of all branch second derivatives gives strict convexity/unique interior minimizer; top-r eigenframe proves exact alpha=2/T_r threshold; right-factor support proves rank nonincrease. Independent rational permutation calculations establish the H=(1,10,11),r=2,alpha=2/25 value 573/625 and alpha=1/12 optimum 11/12, and check other rational spectra. These are checks, not a replacement for the Birkhoff argument.
